extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, newsroom writers covering diverse communities
extracted.subtask_description: A newsroom style guide listing preferred terminology and cautions for reporting about race, ethnicity, religion, disability, gender and other identity-related topics. Guidance is aimed at word choice, when to identify people by a characteristic, and culturally sensitive usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: bipolar disorder
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and clinical characterization of bipolar disorder (formerly manic depression).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to someone as having bipolar disorder only if it is central to the story and a licensed medical professional has formally diagnosed the person. Do not use 'bipolar' as an adjective for something that rapidly or drastically changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: biracial, multiracial, mixed-race, two or more races
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinctions among biracial (two races), multiracial (two or more racial backgrounds) and related terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred terms include multiracial, biracial, multiethnic, polyethnic. Use 'mixed' and 'mixed-race' with caution because some people find them offensive; others embrace them.

rubrics_metrics.name: bisexual, bi
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of bisexual: capacity for enduring physical, romantic and/or emotional attractions to same and other genders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: People do not need specific sexual experiences to be bisexual; they may identify regardless of sexual history. Use person-first, accurate descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black church
rubrics_metrics.description: Collective noun for Christian churches with predominantly Black membership and clerical leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refers generally to Protestant denominations and has been a major institutional foundation in the Black community. 'Black churches' (plural) may be more accurate in some contexts; be mindful many Black people belong to churches not predominantly Black.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black Codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-Civil War statutes (1865–1866) curtailing rights of African Americans in Reconstruction-era South.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also called Negro Codes; enacted to restore political/economic structures of slavery, e.g., forbidding Black people from owning or renting farmland.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black leader
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage caution around labeling someone 'Black leader.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using the term because it implies one person speaks for all Black people. Instead identify the person's organization or role when referring to a local Black person in leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black Lives Matter, #BlackLivesMatter
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of the movement and its origins as a Twitter hashtag and civil rights campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe movement's aims (oppose police violence, advance racial justice). Note that the group says it does not believe Black lives are more important than others and that it stands with other oppressed peoples; explain context and claims accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black Muslim
rubrics_metrics.description: Term associated historically with Nation of Islam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered derogatory and should be avoided. Preferred: member of the Nation of Islam; do not use 'Black Muslim' to describe African-Americans practicing traditional Islam—say 'African-American Muslims' instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black or African American, U.S. Census definition of
rubrics_metrics.description: Census Bureau definition: origins in any of the Black racial groups of Africa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that census racial categories reflect social definitions, not biological/anthropological/genetic definitions; categories may include racial and national origin or sociocultural groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black Twitter
rubrics_metrics.description: A virtual community on Twitter focused on issues of interest to the Black community (particularly U.S.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a tool for social activism including organizing protest rallies and boycotts; contextualize its role in stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: blind/limited vision/low vision/partially sighted/visually impaired
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and preferred terminology for people with varying degrees of vision loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'blind' only when person has complete loss of sight and 'legally blind' when acuity is 20/200 or less unless the person prefers another term. Otherwise use low vision, limited vision, partially sighted or visually impaired and ask individuals their preference. Note regional differences (e.g., 'partially sighted' common in Britain).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bollywood
rubrics_metrics.description: Term for the Hindi-language film industry centered in Mumbai (formerly Bombay).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable popular term for Hindi cinema; note Bollywood is not the only source of Indian cinema and that movies are made in many languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: boomer
rubrics_metrics.description: Refers to people born 1946–1964 (post-WWII baby boom).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Boomers' and 'boomer generation' are preferred over 'baby boomers' (which can be condescending). Avoid lumping them together unless relevant comparisons are being made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boricua
rubrics_metrics.description: Term derived from Borikén (indigenous name for Puerto Rico) conveying pride in Puerto Rican origins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to refer to Puerto Rican identity and cultural pride; provides historical background.

rubrics_metrics.name: born-again
rubrics_metrics.description: Religious term describing a personal transformational Christian experience emphasized by Evangelical Protestants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because it associates someone with a particular religious tradition, do not label someone 'born-again Christian' — let the person self-identify (e.g., 'who calls herself a born-again Christian').

rubrics_metrics.name: Borscht Belt
rubrics_metrics.description: Informal term for Catskills summer resorts that catered to Ashkenazic Jewish families mid-20th century.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide cultural and historical context; avoid stereotyping and note significance to Jewish entertainers and culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Buddha
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and pronunciation guidance for 'Buddha' (Siddhartha Gautama).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pronounced 'BUD-dah' (short u); 'the Buddha' means 'the awakened one' and a Buddha is anyone who has attained enlightenment; distinguish historic and celestial Buddhas as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Buddhism
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of Buddhism's origins, major teachings, and principal branches (Theravada, Mahayana, Vajrayana).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting, note differences among major forms/vehicles, their geographic distribution and distinct emphases (e.g., monastic focus in Theravada, universality in Mahayana, Tibetan Vajrayana practices).

rubrics_metrics.name: burkini
rubrics_metrics.description: A modest swimsuit covering arms, legs and hair worn by some Muslim women.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the term origin (burqa + bikini) and context (modesty/faith). When relevant, report on controversies (e.g., 2016 French bans) with factual context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burmese names
rubrics_metrics.description: General naming conventions: often two one-syllable names plus honorifics; complexity and use of honorifics like Daw, U, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check and use appropriate honorifics and name order; local customs vary and should be respected.

rubrics_metrics.name: burqa
rubrics_metrics.description: An all-enveloping outer garment with a mesh-covered opening for the eyes, most commonly found in Afghanistan and Pakistan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define accurately and link to related garments (abaya, hijab, niqab); avoid conflating distinct garments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cajun, Creole
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions distinguishing Cajun (descendants of Acadian French immigrants to Louisiana) and Creole (person of European parentage born in West Indies/Central America/Gulf States).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specific terms appropriately based on heritage, culture and region; be precise rather than generic labeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cambodian names
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical name order and conventions: family name first, personal name second; middle names are rare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect name order and verify preferences with subjects when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cantonese
rubrics_metrics.description: A Chinese dialect spoken mainly around Guangzhou (Canton) and in Hong Kong; not spoken by all Chinese people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume all Chinese speak Cantonese; distinguish Cantonese from Mandarin and other dialects in reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: caste
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical social hierarchy in India rooted in Hindu scriptures and later hereditary and oppressive structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain caste's historical role, present-day effects (segregation, discrimination), and that while many legal changes have reduced its formal power, caste-based prejudice persists in social interactions and policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: caste system
rubrics_metrics.description: More detailed description of the varna and jati divisions, restrictions on mobility, and the creation of 'untouchables' (Scheduled Castes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report that caste discrimination is illegal in India yet persists; note contemporary policy responses such as quotas/affirmative action and resulting tensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catholic, catholic
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalized 'Catholic' refers to Roman Catholic Church; lowercase 'catholic' means universal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify denominational distinctions (Roman Catholic vs. Eastern Catholic churches) and avoid conflating Eastern Catholics with Orthodox. Use 'Roman Catholic' when a distinction among denominations is needed; do not call Eastern Catholics 'Orthodox.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Caucasian
rubrics_metrics.description: Term historically used in demographic contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using 'Caucasian' as a synonym for White except in demographic data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central America
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographic definition of the isthmus connecting North and South America and the seven constituent countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use correct geographic terms and list the seven countries (Belize, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, Panama) when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: cerebral palsy
rubrics_metrics.description: Neurological disorders appearing in infancy or early childhood affecting movement and coordination; not caused by muscle or nerve problems but by brain abnormalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is acceptable to describe someone as 'a person with cerebral palsy' followed by an explanation of what the condition entails if relevant. Ask subjects their preferred terms when describing specific symptoms. Avoid derogatory shorthand like 'spaz' even if referring to spastic cerebral palsy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chabad
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization of the Chabad-Lubavitch movement of Hasidic Judaism focused on outreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the correct organizational name and provide context about outreach emphasis and Hasidic origins where pertinent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chaldeans
rubrics_metrics.description: Catholics from Iraq; a religious and ethnic minority with U.S. communities (largest in Detroit and San Diego areas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish Chaldean Catholic identity and historical ties to Roman Catholic Church; avoid conflating with other Semitic groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charlie Chan
rubrics_metrics.description: A fictional detective created in 1925 whose portrayal became a stereotype and was often played by white actors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caution: the character's portrayal employs racial stereotyping (inscrutable dialogue, phonetic speech patterns). Use this as an example of harmful stereotypes and avoid replicating such caricatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chican@
rubrics_metrics.description: An inclusive spelling meant to represent both Chicano/Chicana and allow readers to choose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in some academic department names; the '@' ending simultaneously presents masculine and feminine endings. See Latin@ for related usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chicana, Chicano
rubrics_metrics.description: People of Mexican descent; 'Chicano' for men and 'Chicana' for women. Terms were reclaimed during the Chicano movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand historical context and pride in indigenous ancestry; use terms appropriately and in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: chief
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple meanings: leader of a people or highest-ranking official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When referring to Indigenous leaders, ensure 'chief' is appropriate and actually used by that group; never use as a nickname for a Native man. Be cautious of slang/colloquial uses that perpetuate stereotypes. The word is acceptable in other contexts (chief executive, military titles) but sensitivity is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: china doll
rubrics_metrics.description: Figurine image used metaphorically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caution: when used to describe women of Chinese/Asian heritage it demeans them by implying submissiveness or sexualization; consider avoiding the metaphor and be mindful of 'Dragon Lady' reverse image stereotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chinaman
rubrics_metrics.description: An historical slur for Chinese people deriving from 19th-century U.S. contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the term; it is a slur. Do not use or repeat except in historical quotations with clear context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chinese laundries
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical reference to Chinese-run laundries in 19th–20th century America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caution: can be racially charged; if used, provide historical context about discrimination and stereotyping rather than perpetuating tropes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chinese names
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical name order is family name first, personal name second; habit of adopting Western names and other variations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check an interview subject's preference for name order, hyphenation or adoption of Western names; avoid assuming Western ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: ching-chong
rubrics_metrics.description: Derogatory slur mocking Asian languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the term; do not repeat except in clear critical context or historical reporting that condemns the phrase.

rubrics_metrics.name: chink
rubrics_metrics.description: A slur targeting people of Asian heritage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the term; also avoid idiomatic uses like 'chink in the armor' that can evoke the slur despite a non-racial original meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chitlin' Circuit
rubrics_metrics.description: Touring route and network of venues that supported Black entertainers during the Jim Crow era.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain its cultural significance in providing safe venues and fostering musical genres; avoid romanticizing without context about the discrimination that necessitated it.

rubrics_metrics.name: chopsticks
rubrics_metrics.description: Utensils originating in China and used across East and parts of Southeast Asia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note origins (China ~1200 B.C.) and regional adoption; do not assume all Asian cultures use chopsticks (e.g., many Indonesians, Thais, Indians do not traditionally use them).

rubrics_metrics.name: Christianity
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of Christianity as the world's largest religion based on Jesus and the New Testament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide basic doctrinal context, historical development, and the diversity among Christian denominations when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred usage and naming guidance for the denomination often referred to as the Mormon Church.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the full official name on first reference; preferred shortened references include 'the Church' or 'the Church of Jesus Christ.' Avoid 'Mormon Church,' 'LDS Church,' 'LDS' or 'Mormon' as substitutes for the church name; when referring to members use 'members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints' or 'Latter-day Saints.' Use 'Mormon' only in proper names like 'Book of Mormon' or historical adjective uses. Note that the church asks journalists to avoid 'Mormon' usage and provide background on beliefs and structure when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cinco de Mayo
rubrics_metrics.description: Mexican holiday commemorating the 1862 Battle of Puebla (May 5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the U.S. it is often a celebration of Mexican culture; not equivalent to Mexican Independence Day (Sept. 16). Provide correct historical context and avoid conflating holidays.

rubrics_metrics.name: cisgender, cis
rubrics_metrics.description: Term describing people whose gender identity aligns with sex assigned at birth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain roots of the prefix 'cis-' (Latin 'on the same side as') and note that a more widely understood phrase is 'non-transgender people.' 'Cisgender' may be shortened to 'cis.' Avoid implying cisgender is the neutral/normal state.

rubrics_metrics.name: civil rights movement, Civil Rights Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Broad historical reference to struggles to end segregation and discrimination in U.S. from ~1945–1970 and legislative outcomes like the Civil Rights Act (1964) and Voting Rights Act (1965).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting, ground references in specific events, legislation and timelines (e.g., Montgomery bus boycott, March on Washington). Avoid vague or ahistorical uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: civil union
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal status giving some rights similar to marriage, recognized by some states but not the U.S. government historically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note legal distinctions from marriage and the 2015 Supreme Court decision legalizing same-sex marriage nationwide; refer to related terms (commitment ceremony, domestic partner) as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: classism
rubrics_metrics.description: Prejudice and discriminatory actions based on socioeconomic status and class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the term to describe systemic bias by upper classes against lower socioeconomic groups and provide concrete examples where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: closed captions
rubrics_metrics.description: Text display of all audible information in a video intended for Deaf or hard-of-hearing audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include captions of spoken words plus descriptions of loud noises, sound effects and music; distinguish closed captions from other accessibility features when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: closeted, in the closet
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes a person not open about sexual orientation or gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer phrasing like 'not out about being [lesbian/gay/etc.]' Recognize that people may be out to some but not others; be sensitive to the reasons for secrecy (fear, safety, job loss).

rubrics_metrics.name: cochlear implant
rubrics_metrics.description: An electronic device that can help some people who are deaf or hard of hearing to perceive sounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid describing it as a corrective device that fully restores hearing or as something that 'returns' a person to mainstream society. Define it as an electronic device that assists in understanding speech and note cultural controversies within the Deaf community.

rubrics_metrics.name: code switching
rubrics_metrics.description: Changing speech or behavior depending on context; within Black community often refers to shifting between African American Language and Standard English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain that code switching is a learned social skill and not automatic; avoid framing it as deficiency and acknowledge structural factors (education, teachers, exposure) that influence mastery.

rubrics_metrics.name: coded language
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of seemingly race-neutral terms that mask explicit or implicit bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples (e.g., 'inner-city', 'urban') and explain how such terms can be code for race, people of color, or low-income groups; encourage reporters to call out bias rather than rely on euphemisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: codeswitching
rubrics_metrics.description: Shifting between languages, dialects, accents or behaviors to adapt to situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar to code switching entry; differentiate language-switching from other forms of social adaptation and provide contextual examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: codger
rubrics_metrics.description: Ageist term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using ageist slurs or pejorative labels for older people.

rubrics_metrics.name: colonialism
rubrics_metrics.description: European imperial expansion from the Age of Exploration that led to subjugation of peoples in Asia, Africa and the Americas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide historical context, name colonial powers and effects; link to related terms like imperialism and Third World in appropriate reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: colored
rubrics_metrics.description: Archaic term for Black people; in some countries denotes mixed ancestry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use except in historical references, official names, or direct quotes; prefer modern terms such as Black or African American where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: colorism
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference for lighter skin over darker skin within racial groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how colorism operates within and across races (e.g., 'brown paper bag test') and its social consequences; include historical examples where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: coming out
rubrics_metrics.description: Short for 'coming out of the closet' — disclosing one's sexual orientation or gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as an explanatory phrase; cross-reference terms like closeted/in the closet and outing; be sensitive to privacy and safety concerns in reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: commitment ceremony
rubrics_metrics.description: A marriage-like ceremony without legal status; participants may be same-sex or different-sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify that such ceremonies may be religiously recognized but are not legally binding; cross-reference civil union and domestic partner.

rubrics_metrics.name: community
rubrics_metrics.description: Term often used as a catch-all for groups with shared traits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'community' with caution—it's a cliché and implies shared opinion that cannot be assumed. Avoid vague labels like 'the Korean community' or 'white community leaders'; instead identify groups and leaders by name and, when possible, size or scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confucianism
rubrics_metrics.description: A philosophy developed by Confucius emphasizing social harmony and moral obligation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat it as a philosophy rather than a religion; provide basic explanatory context when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: congenital disability
rubrics_metrics.description: A disability present at birth (e.g., Down syndrome, congenital heart conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer phrasing like 'a person with a congenital disability' or 'was born with a disability.' Name a specific disability only when pertinent and avoid using terms like 'defect' or 'birth' which imply incompleteness.

rubrics_metrics.name: continuing care retirement community
rubrics_metrics.description: Communities offering independent living, assisted living and skilled nursing care, often under long-term contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the continuum of housing/services and typical contractual arrangements when relevant to reporting about elder care.

rubrics_metrics.name: convict
rubrics_metrics.description: Label for someone who is incarcerated or has been convicted of a crime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using 'convict' as a label; prefer people-first language (e.g., 'a person who is incarcerated' or 'a person convicted of').
